primary_meaning: Distant Gentile nations or remote coastlands of the earth that will receive God's law and salvation

alternatives.meaning: Sites of isolation, exile, or separation (literal or spiritual)
basis: geographic isolation motif in prophetic and apostolic settings

alternatives.meaning: Elements of creation that flee or vanish under divine judgment
Arenas of missionary advance or temporary refuge for the gospel
The church as solid ground amid the chaotic sea of the world
basis: allegorical extensions of sea = nations/chaos imagery

notes: The Hebrew ʾiyyîm (often rendered “isles”/“islands”/“coastlands”) is treated in standard Christian biblical interpretation primarily as a prophetic metonym for far-off Gentile peoples rather than a freestanding typological symbol. Literal geographic references and eschatological instability motifs are secondary but well-attested; highly allegorical church-as-island readings remain marginal.
